name: Wattenberg
kurzbeschreibung: Original mountain settlement above Wattens with ancient farmhouses and a dreamy panoramic view over the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The mountain municipality of Wattenberg is situated at an elevation of 1,050 metres above sea level in the Watten Valley within the Tux Alps, located in the Innsbruck-Land district south above the Inn Valley. Home to approximately 750 residents, Wattenberg is the highest-altitude municipality in the district. The extensive municipal area spans more than 67 square kilometres, reaching from precipitous farmsteads through ancient Swiss stone pine woodlands up to the Lizumer Reckner at 2,886 metres, the highest peak in the Tux Alps. The settlement consists primarily of scattered historic farmhouses clinging to sunny, steep slopes. Wattenberg is home to the Austrian Armed Forces' Lizum Walchen military training area and is celebrated by hikers, mountaineers, and ski tourers as one of the most pristine alpine valleys in the Eastern Alps.

Geschichte

Permanent settlement in the steep Watten Valley began in the High Middle Ages through the establishment of pastoral estate farms ('Schwaighöfe') paying tithes to the Hall Collegiate Convent and Stams Abbey. The village was officially documented in 1267 under the name 'Watenáerperge'. During the 15th and 16th centuries, the community experienced an economic upswing with copper and iron ore mining in the Mölstal and Knappenkuchl areas. To educate the children of miners and farmers, an independent village school was founded as early as 1524—more than two centuries before general compulsory schooling was instituted in Austria, commemorated by a schoolboy on the municipal coat of arms. Rather than a central parish church, local farmers erected eleven historic wayside chapels across the mountainsides, alongside the high-altitude Christ the King chapel built in 1961 at the military camp.

Anreise

Travel to Wattenberg proceeds via the central Inn Valley in Tyrol. Motorists leave the Inntal Autobahn A12 at the Wattens exit or travel along federal highway B171. From central Wattens, the winding L242 Wattenberg provincial road climbs steeply for five kilometres up to the municipal centre. Visitors heading deeper into the valley towards the Wattentaler Lizum continue along the mountain road to the designated public car park at Walchen (1,410 metres), beyond which private vehicular traffic is prohibited. Rail passengers travel via S-Bahn Tirol to the Fritzens-Wattens railway station, connecting to the VVT on-demand Regiotax service (line 525T). In addition, licensed mountain taxi services operate from the station or Walchen directly to the Lizumer Hütte.

Tipps

The centrepiece for alpine enthusiasts is the high-altitude Wattentaler Lizum and the historic Lizumer Hütte (2,019 metres), a key mountain base on the Eagle Walk (Adlerweg) and the Munich-Venice trail. Nature enthusiasts revere the Lizumer Zirbenweg, a panoramic path winding through one of the oldest and most extensive Swiss stone pine forests in the Eastern Alps. In winter, the cirques around the Geier (2,857 m) and Lizumer Reckner (2,886 m) offer legendary ski touring routes. Culturally minded walkers can explore the signposted Wattenberg Chapel Trail connecting eleven lovingly maintained domestic shrines. Hikers should check firing schedules for the Lizum Walchen military training grounds, which open freely to the public during non-training periods.
